lesson.content:
## What it is
Data communication is the exchange of data between two devices over a transmission medium such as a cable or radio waves. For it to work, the devices must be part of a communication system made of hardware and software. [p. 1]

## Real-life analogy
Imagine a walkie-talkie. You can only talk to your friend who is also using a walkie-talkie, and you can only hear them. This is similar to data communication, where devices can only communicate with devices that are part of the same system. [p. 1]

## How it works
1. **Message**: The information to be sent, such as text, numbers, pictures, audio, or video. [p. 1]
2. **Sender**: The device that sends the message, like a computer or a phone. [p. 1]
3. **Receiver**: The device that receives the message. [p. 1]
4. **Transmission medium**: The physical path the message travels, such as twisted pair cable, fiber, or radio waves. [p. 1]
5. **Protocol**: The set of rules both sides agree on. Without a protocol, two devices may be connected but cannot understand each other. [p. 1]

## Key terms
- **Message**: The information to be sent, such as text, numbers, pictures, audio, or video. [p. 1]
- **Sender**: The device that sends the message, like a computer or a phone. [p. 1]
- **Receiver**: The device that receives the message. [p. 1]
- **Transmission medium**: The physical path the message travels, such as twisted pair cable, fiber, or radio waves. [p. 1]
- **Protocol**: The set of rules both sides agree on. Without a protocol, two devices may be connected but cannot understand each other. [p. 1]

## Example
A simple example of data communication is a computer sending an email to another computer. The message (the email) travels through the transmission medium (the internet) using a protocol (SMTP, the Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) until it reaches the receiver (the other computer). [p. 1]

## What to draw in the exam
No diagram needed. [p. 1]

## Exam tip
Examiners usually ask about the components of data communication and how they work together. Make sure to understand the roles of the sender, receiver, and transmission medium, as well as the importance of the protocol. [p. 1]
